summary: Viewed all four supplied actual PNGs, including native 1x and the supplied nearest-neighbor 3x views on light, dark and checker backgrounds. The small quadruped, short left tail, olive neck and feet, and broad gray-brown stone shell remain recognizable. The upper-left highlights, darker right shell face and lower rim distinguish the dome from its side; shell plates read as stone. No obvious unintended transparent holes or broken neck/limb connections are visible. Near feet support the body at the common baseline; the small elevated far feet read as overlapping limbs. Windup shortens the neck and gathers the legs, move extends the rear leg, attack tucks the head and advances the forefoot beneath a broader shell shoulder, and recover restores the stance. Idle changes are subtle, but shell identity and limb attachment remain consistent. The low flattened dead shell is distinguishable from the taller tucked sleeping shell. The last nine frames show readable authored states: cyan energy follows shell grooves in skill_a, three stone fragments rise from cyan roots on the actual shell in skill_b, and skill_c leaves fading grit and reduced groove energy. The shell is the specified skill source, so a hand, mouth or weapon attachment is not applicable. Poison combines a lowered stance with purple bubbles, stun combines a withdrawn head with gold sparks, and sleep tucks the body toward the ground; these are more than palette tints. Head/eye detail and paired status-frame changes are small at 1x. This is an advisory visual recommendation, not the user selection. Static pose previews cannot establish playback timing, smoothness, actual battle contact, or runtime grounding, and PNGs alone cannot verify literal-grid authorship or the author model.
